text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they have been getting worse over time?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury—jerking your finger while it's extended—strongly suggests a specific type of ligament damage. Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and is the tip of your finger crooked or tilted compared to your other fingers?

text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Avulsion Fracture of the Distal Phalanx of the Right Ring Finger (Jersey Finger).
